newsitem.title: USA: Global DirectMail stock falls on profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: Global DirectMail stock falls on profit outlook.

text.p: Global DirectMail Corp.'s stock plunged more than 27 percent Tuesday after the mail-order marketer of office and computer supplies said it expected to report flat first-quarter profits and analysts downgraded the company.

The stock dropped $7.75 to $20.75 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, making it the biggest percentage loser on the exchange. Trading in the stock was halted briefly at midday.
The Port Washington, N.Y.-based company said it expected first-quarter net income to be in line with profits posted in last year's fourth and first quarters.
Global DirectMail reported net income of $11.8 million, or 31 cents per share, for the fourth quarter of 1996 and $11.39 million, or 31 cents per share, in the first quarter of last year.
Wall Street analysts surveyed by the First Call service on average were predicting net income of 36 cents a share for the first quarter of 1997.

Earlier, Montgomery Securities said analysts Tom Courtney and Kevin Dede cut their first-quarter and 1997 earnings estimates for the company, saying the strong dollar would hurt overseas sales. The analysts maintained their "buy" rating on the stock.
Global DirectMail said in a news release it knew of no reason for the decline in its stock price. It said it expected growth in sales vs. the fourth quarter.
"The fundamentals of the company's business remain strong," Global DirectMail said in the statement.
The company sells brand-name and private-label computer, office and industrial supplies.
